name: The International System for Reporting Serous Fluid Cytopathology (TIS / ISRSFC)
specimen: Pleural, peritoneal (ascitic), pericardial fluids and peritoneal washings
use: Peritoneal washings can be reported using these categories, with staging context (TIS includes a washing chapter).
not_use: CSF, synovial fluid, cyst fluids, BAL (report descriptively/other systems).
Do not use to diagnose mesothelioma without ancillary support.
report_structure: Ancillary results (IHC on cell block, flow, FISH)

adequacy.title: Volume and processing
items: Minimum 50–75 mL recommended for pleural fluid; larger volumes do not further increase sensitivity substantially.
Fresh specimen or refrigerated at 4 °C if delayed (stable up to ~2 weeks); no fixative needed.
Prepare cytospin/smears + cell block routinely for ancillary testing.
No numeric cellularity threshold – adequacy is a judgement; presence of mesothelial cells/macrophages confirms sampling of the space.

categories.name: Non-diagnostic
categories.definition: Insufficient cellular material for interpretation (e.g. acellular, only blood, degenerated/obscured cells). Very rare in serous fluids.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Repeat analysis if clinical suspicion persists; ensure adequate volume (≥75 mL) and fresh/refrigerated specimen.
criteria: Acellular or paucicellular specimen with no mesothelial cells/macrophages (sampling of wrong space).
Marked degeneration, drying, or obscuring blood precluding evaluation.
Use only after excluding processing issues; a few benign cells generally qualify as NFM.

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – acellular/insufficient
diagnoses.final: Non-diagnostic. The specimen is acellular/insufficient for cytological evaluation.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat sampling with adequate volume (≥75 mL suggested for pleural fluid) is recommended if clinically indicated.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: ND (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic – degenerated/obscured
diagnoses.final: Non-diagnostic. Cells are poorly preserved/obscured by blood.
diagnoses.comment: Send fresh specimen promptly or refrigerated (4 °C) for repeat analysis.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: ND (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Negative for malignancy
categories.definition: Benign/reactive elements only, with or without specific benign findings.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Clinical follow-up; investigate cause of effusion. Repeat cytology if suspicion of malignancy remains.
criteria: Reactive mesothelial cells (singly, small groups, 'windows', two-tone cytoplasm, binucleation), macrophages, inflammatory cells.
Specific benign entities may be named (e.g. lymphocytic, eosinophilic, LE cells, rheumatoid pattern, organisms).
No population of 'foreign' cells; second population absent.

diagnoses.name: Reactive mesothelial cells, macrophages and inflammatory cells
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Reactive mesothelial cells, macrophages and mixed inflammatory cells.
diagnoses.comment: No malignant cells seen. Correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Lymphocyte-rich effusion (e.g. tuberculosis, post-CABG, chronic)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Lymphocyte-rich effusion.
diagnoses.comment: Predominantly small mature lymphocytes. Consider tuberculosis (ADA, GeneXpert/culture); if monotonous or atypical, flow cytometry to exclude lymphoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Eosinophilic effusion (>10% eosinophils)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Eosinophilic effusion.
diagnoses.comment: Often associated with air/blood in pleural space (pneumothorax, trauma, prior tap), drugs, parasites, Churg–Strauss. Clinical correlation advised.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Neutrophil-rich/suppurative effusion (empyema, parapneumonic)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Acute inflammatory (neutrophil-rich) effusion.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest culture and biochemical correlation (pH, glucose, LDH).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Rheumatoid pleuritis pattern
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Features consistent with rheumatoid pleuritis.
diagnoses.comment: Elongated/spindle histiocytes, multinucleated giant cells and granular necrotic background; correlate with rheumatoid serology.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Lupus pleuritis (LE cells)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. LE cells identified; findings compatible with lupus serositis in proper clinical setting.
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with ANA/anti-dsDNA.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Endometriosis
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Findings may represent endometriosis (haemosiderin-laden macrophages ± endometrial-type cells).
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Organisms / infection (fungi, parasites, e.g. Strongyloides, microfilaria)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. [Organism] identified.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation and microbiological confirmation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Benign elements – peritoneal washing (Müllerian/endosalpingiosis, benign mesothelium)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Benign mesothelial cells (± benign Müllerian-type epithelium/endosalpingiosis with psammoma bodies).
diagnoses.comment: Peritoneal washings with endosalpingiosis can mimic serous neoplasia; correlate with histology.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Contaminants (skin squames, cartilage, hepatocytes, bowel content)
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Sampling contaminants noted.
diagnoses.comment: Contaminants related to sampling path; bowel contents may indicate inadvertent bowel puncture/perforation – inform clinician.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Extramedullary haematopoiesis / megakaryocytes
diagnoses.final: Negative for malignancy. Extramedullary haematopoiesis present.
diagnoses.comment: Seen in myelofibrosis or contamination by bone marrow; correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: NFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Atypia of undetermined significance
categories.definition: Cells with atypia insufficient for SFM or MAL, most often reactive mesothelial atypia vs well-differentiated malignancy that cannot be resolved.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Repeat cytology with ancillary tests (cell block IHC: calretinin/WT1/D2-40 vs Ber-EP4/MOC-31/Claudin-4; BAP1, MTAP, CDKN2A FISH); clinical/radiological correlation. Lab AUS rate ideally <10%.
criteria: Mild–moderate nuclear atypia in a few cells, especially in presence of inflammation/ascites of cirrhosis.
Atypical lymphoid cells with insufficient material for flow cytometry.
Avoid as a 'wastebasket'; explain the reason for atypia in the comment.

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical mesothelial cells (reactive vs neoplastic)
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance. Atypical mesothelial cells present.
diagnoses.comment: Reactive mesothelial atypia vs mesothelioma cannot be distinguished on this material. Suggest repeat sampling with cell block for BAP1/MTAP IHC and clinico-radiological correlation.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical epithelioid cells, few
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance. Few atypical epithelioid cells of uncertain nature.
diagnoses.comment: Insufficient for further characterisation; repeat fluid with cell block for IHC suggested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: AUS – atypical lymphoid cells
diagnoses.final: Atypia of undetermined significance. Atypical lymphoid population.
diagnoses.comment: Repeat sample with flow cytometry recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Suspicious for malignancy
categories.definition: Features strongly suggestive of malignancy but quantitatively/qualitatively insufficient, or ancillary studies not available/confirmatory.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Ancillary studies on cell block/additional fluid; tissue biopsy (pleural biopsy/thoracoscopy) as needed.
criteria: Few highly atypical cells or second population suspicious for carcinoma.
Atypical mesothelial proliferation suspicious for mesothelioma without confirmatory BAP1/MTAP loss or CDKN2A deletion.
Lymphoid population suspicious for lymphoma without flow/IHC confirmation.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for metastatic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy – suspicious for metastatic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: A small population of atypical epithelial cells suspicious for carcinoma is present; IHC on cell block/repeat sample recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for mesothelioma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy – atypical mesothelial proliferation, suspicious for mesothelioma.
diagnoses.comment: Recommend BAP1/MTAP IHC and/or CDKN2A FISH, and tissue correlation (pleural biopsy).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious for malignancy – suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry and IHC on cell block recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

categories.name: Malignant (primary or secondary)
categories.definition: Unequivocal malignancy. Primary: mesothelioma, primary effusion lymphoma. Secondary: metastatic carcinoma, lymphoma/leukaemia, melanoma, sarcoma, germ cell tumours, etc.

rom.source: TIS book 2020 (figures derived from Farahani & Baloch, Diagn Cytopathol 2019, doi 10.1002/dc.24278: 17.4/20.7/65.9/81.8/98.9%)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies/19,128 cases (Cancer Cytopathol 2024, doi 10.1002/cncy.22822) – pooled (95% CI)
Meta-analysis, 16 studies (Jamal, Vey et al., 2024) – pooled (95% CI)

categories.management: Oncology referral. Use cell block for IHC/predictive biomarkers (e.g. ER/PR/HER2, EGFR/ALK/PD-L1, MMR).
criteria: Metastatic adenocarcinoma: second 'foreign' population, 3-D 'cannonball'/papillary/acinar clusters, cytoplasmic vacuoles, signet-ring cells; MOC-31/Ber-EP4/Claudin-4+.
Mesothelioma: numerous mesothelial cells, large morula-like groups with knobby borders, cell-in-cell, macronucleoli; confirm with loss of BAP1/MTAP or CDKN2A homozygous deletion.
Lymphoma: monotonous dispersed lymphoid cells, lymphoglandular bodies; flow cytometry.
Squamous carcinoma, small cell carcinoma, melanoma, sarcoma, germ cell tumour.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic adenocarcinoma (specify likely primary)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic adenocarcinoma, [IHC profile consistent with primary in lung/breast/ovary/GI tract].
diagnoses.comment: IHC on cell block: [list]. Predictive biomarkers can be performed on the cell block if requested.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic breast carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic carcinoma, consistent with breast primary (GATA3+, ER+).
diagnoses.comment: ER/PR/HER2 can be done on the cell block.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic lung adenocarcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic adenocarcinoma, consistent with lung primary (TTF1+, Napsin A+).
diagnoses.comment: Cell block suitable for EGFR/ALK/ROS1/PD-L1 testing.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma (Müllerian)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma, consistent with Müllerian (tubo-ovarian/peritoneal) origin (PAX8+, WT1+, aberrant p53).
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with CA-125 and imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic gastrointestinal/pancreatobiliary adenocarcinoma (incl. signet-ring)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic adenocarcinoma, consistent with GI/pancreatobiliary origin (CK20+, CDX2+, SATB2±).
diagnoses.comment: Correlate with endoscopy/imaging.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma (p40+).
diagnoses.comment: Search for primary (lung, cervix, head and neck, oesophagus).
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic small cell / neuroendocrine carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic small cell carcinoma (synaptophysin/INSM1+).
diagnoses.comment: Most commonly lung primary.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic melanoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic melanoma (SOX10/S100/HMB45/Melan-A+).
diagnoses.comment: Melanin pigment may be absent (amelanotic); correlate with history of cutaneous/ocular melanoma. BRAF testing can be done on the cell block.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma/leukaemia involving effusion
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Involvement by [lymphoma type/leukaemia].
diagnoses.comment: Flow cytometry/IHC performed/recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Metastatic sarcoma / germ cell tumour / other
diagnoses.final: Malignant – secondary: Metastatic [sarcoma/germ cell tumour].
diagnoses.comment: IHC and clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Secondary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Mesothelioma (epithelioid)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – primary: Malignant cells consistent with mesothelioma (epithelioid type).
diagnoses.comment: Mesothelial phenotype (calretinin/WT1/D2-40+, Claudin-4/MOC-31−) with BAP1 loss and/or MTAP loss/CDKN2A deletion. Clinico-radiological correlation recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Primary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Primary effusion lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant – primary: Primary effusion lymphoma (HHV8+).
diagnoses.comment: Large plasmablastic/immunoblastic cells, CD45±, CD138+, HHV8 (LANA)+; usually HIV setting.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Primary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

diagnoses.name: Fluid overload–associated large B-cell lymphoma (HHV8-negative)
diagnoses.final: Malignant – primary: Large B-cell lymphoma in effusion, HHV8-negative (fluid overload-associated large B-cell lymphoma).
diagnoses.comment: WHO-HAEM5 entity; usually elderly with fluid overload.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: MAL – Primary (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)
diagnoses.note: WHO-HAEM5 (2022) term; not in TIS 2020 book.

diagnoses.name: Well-differentiated papillary mesothelial tumour
diagnoses.final: Report descriptively – papillary mesothelial proliferation; not reliably diagnosed on fluid.
diagnoses.comment: Histology required.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: AUS/SFM (International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology)

extra.title: Ancillary panels (cell block)
items: Mesothelial: calretinin, WT1, D2-40, CK5/6, HBME-1.
Epithelial (carcinoma): Claudin-4, MOC-31, Ber-EP4, B72.3, CEA.
Mesothelioma vs reactive: BAP1 loss, MTAP loss, CDKN2A (p16) FISH homozygous deletion; (desmin+ favours reactive, EMA membranous favours malignant – less reliable).
Site-specific: TTF1/Napsin (lung), GATA3/ER (breast), PAX8/WT1 (Müllerian), CDX2/CK20/SATB2 (GI), SOX10 (melanoma).

references: Chandra A, Crothers B, Kurtycz D, Schmitt F (eds). The International System for Serous Fluid Cytopathology. Springer, 2020.
Pooled risk-of-malignancy estimates from published systematic reviews/meta-analyses of TIS categories (2022–2023); figures shown as approximate ranges.
